subject: Medisys RFP: planned key-compromise containment & emergency rotation playbook
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medisys.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Benjamin Taylor <benjamin.taylor@medisys.com>, security@medisys.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Medisys RFP: Key compromise and emergency rotation playbook - initial questions

Diego,

Thanks for sending over the initial RFP attachments. As part of Medisys' procurement security review we need a focused response on your planned process for a confirmed private-key compromise (customer-owned or Redwood-managed keys). Specifically we need answers to the following so we can finalize our technical appendix: 

- What is your guaranteed RTO for a forced emergency key rotation (time from request to all active tokens/CEKs rolled and tombstoned) for a single-region deployment and for a multi-region active-active setup?
- Can you provide technical evidence that private key material cannot be exported from your HSMs after import? We need vendor attestations or test reports.
- For BYOK imports: describe exactly what Redwood stores post-import (wrapped key, key handle, metadata) and whether any plaintext is written to disk or backups at any point.
- How do you propagate a revocation/tombstone across regions and what guarantees exist that stale caches will not be used (session tokens, long-lived CEKs)?
- What forensic artifacts do you produce after an incident (log types, log format, timeline of events) and what is your SLA to provide those artifacts to a customer?
- Please confirm supported HSM import interfaces (PKCS#11, KMIP, vendor-specific) and any constraints on key formats / curves.
- Is there an automated TLS cert/private-key rotation hook if the private key for a serving endpoint is suspected compromised? How do you coordinate with customers on cert provisioning?

We'd like a short playbook summary and a clear statement we can include in our security addendum. If possible, include a minimal sample of the audit events (redacted) so our auditors can validate logging.

Regards,
Claire Thompson
Senior Procurement Manager
Medisys Health

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medisys.com>
Cc: Benjamin Taylor <benjamin.taylor@medisys.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Medisys RFP: Key compromise and emergency rotation playbook - initial questions

Claire — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached our consolidated playbook (redwood_compromise_playbook_v1.2.pdf) plus a small CSV checklist you can plug into procurement. Happy to schedule a technical Q&A tomorrow.

1) Emergency rotation RTO:
- Single-region (warm pool active): typical end-to-end forced rotation is <= 3 minutes for CEK rollover and tombstone propagation to runtime edge caches.
- Multi-region active-active: tombstone propagation is eventually consistent but on average completes within 90 seconds between active regions; full CEK re-encryption of in-flight payloads depends on background job cadence (we push delta re-encryption immediately; typical completion < 30 minutes for large datasets).

2) Export-proof for HSMs:
- We operate with FIPS-validated HSMs (OEM attestation attached in the playbook). Private key material is never exported in plaintext from an HSM once imported. For BYOK imports we only accept wrapped imports or direct HSM-to-HSM import flows. We can provide vendor attestation PDFs under NDA.

3) What Redwood stores after BYOK import:
- Key handle/alias, key metadata (purpose, creation_time, rotation_policy), and the key encrypted/wrapped under an HSM-resident KEK. No plaintext private key material is persisted to disk or backups. The import transaction is logged with a unique txn_id (rot-<uuid>) that appears in the audit trail.

4) Revocation/tombstone propagation:
- We apply a tombstone marker at the key alias level. Tombstones are written to the metadata store and propagated to edge caches via our config pub/sub stack with priority delivery. Edge SDKs validate key state on use; stale cache eviction uses a versioned config with monotonic sequence numbers to prevent rollback. For long-lived sessions we support forced session invalidation and a rekey handshake to prevent reuse of stale CEKs.

5) Forensic artifacts & SLA:
- We produce an incident forensic bundle (redacted by default) that includes JSONL audit logs, timeline entries, HSM transaction logs (where available), and snapshots of key metadata. SLA: evidence package available for delivery within 72 hours of an incident declaration; expedited requests can be prioritized.

6) Supported HSM/import interfaces:
- PKCS#11, KMIP, CloudHSM vendor import, and vendor-specific wrapped import formats. We support RSA, ECDSA (P-256/P-384), and common symmetric key types used for DEKs/CEKs. Details in the attached playbook.

7) TLS cert/private-key rotation hooks:
- Yes. We provide an automated rotation API and webhook model so customers can provide new certs/keys (including customer-generated certs) and trigger zero-downtime rollover. If the private key is suspected compromised, the emergency rotation API also triggers edge cache eviction and client re-handshake directives.

Next steps: I attached the playbook and a small log sample (forensic_log_sample.jsonl). If you want vendor attestations (FIPS/FedRAMP-like statements) we'll send them under the NDA. Marissa — looping you to coordinate procurement collateral.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_compromise_playbook_v1.2.pdf (7.1 MB), playbook_checklist.csv (2 KB), forensic_log_sample.jsonl (10 KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medisys.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Medisys RFP: Key compromise and emergency rotation playbook - technical addendum

Claire — a few technical clarifications and an excerpt from the playbook for your auditors. Happy to expand or redact as needed.

Import semantics and key lifecycle
- Import model: We accept two import flows: (A) direct HSM-to-HSM wrapped import (customer HSM -> Redwood HSM) using vendor-specific import tooling, and (B) customer-supplied wrapped key material (PKCS#12 or KMIP-wrapped) which we ingest via our ingest broker. In both flows the unwrapped private key is never exposed to Redwood-hosted processes.
- Post-import storage: imported keys are persisted as an HSM-wrapped blob and an internal alias pointing to the HSM slot. Backups contain only the wrapped blob; backup restores require the KEK chain present in our active HSM cluster.
- Export restrictions: for all FIPS-validated HSMs we enforce a no-export policy on private key objects. For symmetric CEKs we use envelope encryption — CEKs are wrapped with tenant-specific KEKs that are HSM-resident.

High-velocity compromise containment steps (excerpt)
1) DECLARE INCIDENT: customer or Redwood declares suspected compromise (API flag / SOC ticket).
2) ISOLATE: mark tenant as isolation=read-only for write-heavy operations and disable new token issuance.
3) EMERGENCY_ROTATE(txn_id): call our emergency rotation API which performs:
   - generate new CEKs under tenant KEK (or import new KEK if customer supplies),
   - attach tombstone to old key alias,
   - push tombstone update to edge services (TTL=0 for immediate enforcement),
   - issue reauth directives to SDKs (SDKs will perform key handshake on next call).
4) FORENSIC_SNAPSHOT: collect audit events, HSM transaction identifiers, and system traces into a signed archive.
5) RE-ENCRYPT: background workers perform re-encryption of persisted ciphertext where applicable.
6) CERT_ROTATE (if TLS private key suspected): optionally trigger cert reissue and coordinate with customer CA; our webhook endpoint accepts the new cert/key or a signed CSR.

Operational guarantees and evidence formats
- Logs: JSONL with fields {event_type, actor, key_alias, txn_id, timestamp, region, prev_state, new_state, metadata}. All audit logs are appended to a tamper-evident Merkle chain; signed digests are available for cross-check by an auditor.
- Transaction IDs: every critical operation issues a txn_id (rot-<uuid>) that can be used to replay the causal chain.
- TTLs & propagation: our config pub/sub guarantees at-least-once delivery; tombstone sequence numbers protect against rollbacks. Edge caches validate sequence numbers prior to serving cached ciphertext.

Supported HSM vendors and security posture
- Thales Luna (on-prem and appliance import), AWS CloudHSM (NIST-validated instances), Azure Managed HSM. We also support vendor-specific wrapped import for FIPS-level HSMs.
- We can run attestation flows (remote evidence) for certain vendor hardware; we will provide vendor attestation artifacts under NDA.

Example emergency rotation CLI (redacted)
- curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/keys/emergency-rotate 
  -d '{"tenant_id":"medisys","key_alias":"prod/customer-db-cek","reason":"suspected_exfiltration","force_tombstone":true}'

I'll join the call if you'd like to walk through the API and the sample audit lines.

-Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment note: playbook_checklist.csv contains recommended procurement checklist items (attestation types, sample log fields to request, and SLA language).
